entries.title: About jspassgen | Security Architecture and Principles
entries.content: Skip to main content jspassgen 0.0.19 Menu GitHub Change color theme System About jspassgen jspassgen was created to solve a persistent vulnerability in modern authentication workflows: the reliance on proprietary, cloud-hosted, and telemetry-heavy password generators. Cryptographic Foundation and Formal Specifications jspassgen implements established peer-reviewed cryptographic standards and information-theoretic formulations: Information Entropy: Credential strength is calculated using Claude Shannon's mathematical formulation of entropy: $$\mathcal{H}(X) = -\sum_{i=1}^{n} P(x_i) \log_2 P(x_i)$$ Reference: Shannon, C. E. (1948), "A Mathematical Theory of Communication", Bell System Technical Journal, doi:10.1002/j.1538-7305.1948.tb01338.x. Digital Identity Standards: Password generation strictly conforms to the NIST SP 800-63B Digital Identity Guidelines. jspassgen rejects arbitrary composition rules (such as mandatory special character combinations) in favor of increased length and verified entropy density. Memory-Hard Key Derivation: To neutralize parallel ASIC and GPU brute-force attacks, key derivation utilizes Argon2id as specified in RFC 9106 combined with HKDF key expansion as defined in RFC 5869. Breach Detection via Honeywords: Decoy honeyword generation implements the honeyword canary framework established by Ari Juels and Ronald L. Rivest in "Honeywords: Making password-cracking detectable", ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security (CCS '13), doi:10.1145/2508859.2516671. Passphrase Memorability: Passphrase generation utilizes the curated 7,776-wordlist published by the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF), offering approximately 12.9 bits of entropy per selected word. Architecture Principles Zero External Dependencies: The core generator library contains zero third-party packages, eliminating software supply chain vectors. Strict Local Isolation: Secrets never traverse network sockets. All entropy is sourced directly from hardware CSPRNG interfaces (window.crypto.getRandomValues in browsers, crypto.randomBytes in Node.js). Post-Quantum Bounds: Symmetric entropy thresholds of 256 bits guarantee a minimum of 128 bits of security under Grover's quantum search algorithm. Author and Maintainer Created and maintained by Sebastien Rousseau, Security Engineer and Systems Architect. If an adversary attempts to authenticate with any canary decoy, an immediate intrusion alarm triggers before the genuine master key is exposed. THE PHILOSOPHY Legacy password generators measure length.We measure informational entropy. For three decades, software forced users into artificial composition rules: one uppercase letter, one digit, one symbol. Modern cryptanalysis and GPU clusters crack these predictable patterns in seconds. jspassgen eliminates superstitious rules in favour of Claude Shannon's information theory, post-quantum KDF primitives (RFC 9106 Argon2id and RFC 5869 HKDF), and client-side memory safety. Every secret is mathematically verified before it touches your clipboard. ENGINEERING CAPABILITIESBuilt with cryptographic purity and zero assumptions. Hexagonal isolation, hardware-bound entropy, and verifiable mathematical models engineered for uncompromising long-term security. 01 / QUANTUM HARDENINGResilient against tomorrow's compute. Protects credentials against future quantum decryptors and massively parallel ASIC cracking arrays. Under Grover's algorithm, quantum search provides quadratic speedup (O(√N)), meaning 256 bits of symmetric entropy provides 128 bits of post-quantum security. Paired with memory-hard Argon2id (RFC 9106) and HKDF expansion (RFC 5869), brute-force search remains computationally infeasible.
